+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-14T18:44:29-03:00
+
+    Simplify MOVE damage: named rects and world-space trail.
+
+    Replace the opaque expose arrays and double-subtract path with struct rect
+    helpers (old/new world, trail = old\new, screen map). Underlay paints trail
+    strips only; mover is new footprint only. Add a 1px-left pixel headless test.
+
+<a href=tree-bff2274.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/display.c b/display.c
+index 1b2bf3e..1fc2466 100644
+--- a/display.c
++++ b/display.c
+@@ -1577,107 +1577,159 @@ static void composite_all_except(struct ServerState *srv,
+ }
+ 
+ /*
+- * Window move — design (initial BGCE model; do not “optimize” with FB scroll
+- * of the whole window or full-stack recompose of old∪new):
+- *
+- * Caller: `c` is still at the OLD world position; apply (wdx,wdy) after.
+- *
+- *   1. Expose = old screen rect minus new screen rect (L-shape when the
+- *      box only translates; general difference if size changes).  Exact
+- *      rect_subtract — not ad-hoc strips (strips can miss pixels when
+- *      integer world→screen bounds shift, leaving old window content on
+- *      the wallpaper).
+- *   2. For each expose piece only: composite bottom → top every client
+- *      *except* the mover (wallpaper + windows under + windows above that
+- *      cover the hole).  Overwrites the trail; never leaves mover pixels.
+- *   3. Blit the mover FULL from its buffer at the NEW position only —
+- *      do not re-stack under that body.
+- *   4. Re-blit windows stacked above the mover over old∪new (mover blit
+- *      may have covered them).
+- *
+- * Forbidden regressions:
+- *   - fb_copy_rect_delta / FB scroll of the window body.
+- *   - composite_chain over the entire union of old and new for a move.
+- *   - Expose underlay that skips the wallpaper (c-&gt;next-only when the
+- *     chain is wrong) — leaves “L of old window” on the desktop.
++ * Half-open rectangle: pixels x in [x0, x1), y in [y0, y1).
++ * Used for move damage (world and screen space).
+  */
+-/* Args for parallel MOVE underlay / mover blit (stack-local, join before return). */
+-struct move_underlay_args {
+-	struct ServerState *srv;
+-	const struct Client *skip;
++struct rect {
+ 	int x0, y0, x1, y1;
+ };
+ 
+-struct move_blit_args {
+-	struct ServerState *srv;
+-	const struct Client *cli;
+-	int x0, y0, x1, y1;
+-};
++#define MOVE_TRAIL_MAX 4
+ 
+-static void move_underlay_task(void *arg)
++static struct rect rect_make(int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1)
+ {
+-	struct move_underlay_args *a = arg;
+-	struct Client *stack_dbg;
+-	int nstack = 0;
++	struct rect r = { x0, y0, x1, y1 };
++	return r;
++}
+ 
+-	/* worker id comes from claim hand-out TLS */
+-	bgce_comp_damage_log("underlay", a-&gt;x0, a-&gt;y0, a-&gt;x1, a-&gt;y1, -1);
+-	if (bgce_comp_debug()) {
+-		for (stack_dbg = a-&gt;srv-&gt;clients; stack_dbg; stack_dbg = stack_dbg-&gt;next) {
+-			if (stack_dbg == a-&gt;skip || !stack_dbg-&gt;buffer)
+-				continue;
+-			nstack++;
+-		}
+-		printf("[BGCE] underlay: composite %d layer(s) except skip "
+-		       "id=%u into %dx%d\n",
+-		       nstack,
+-		       a-&gt;skip ? (unsigned)a-&gt;skip-&gt;id : 0,
+-		       a-&gt;x1 - a-&gt;x0, a-&gt;y1 - a-&gt;y0);
+-		fflush(stdout);
+-	}
+-	composite_all_except(a-&gt;srv, a-&gt;skip, a-&gt;x0, a-&gt;y0, a-&gt;x1, a-&gt;y1);
++static int rect_empty(struct rect r)
++{
++	return r.x0 &gt;= r.x1 || r.y0 &gt;= r.y1;
+ }
+ 
+-static void move_blit_task(void *arg)
++static struct rect rect_union(struct rect a, struct rect b)
+ {
+-	struct move_blit_args *a = arg;
+-	const struct Client *cli = a-&gt;cli;
+-
+-	bgce_comp_damage_log("mover", a-&gt;x0, a-&gt;y0, a-&gt;x1, a-&gt;y1, -1);
+-	if (bgce_comp_debug() &amp;&amp; cli) {
+-		uint32_t ww = cli-&gt;world_w ? cli-&gt;world_w : cli-&gt;width;
+-		uint32_t wh = cli-&gt;world_h ? cli-&gt;world_h : cli-&gt;height;
+-
+-		printf("[BGCE] mover: blit id=%u app='%s' world=(%u,%u) %ux%u "
+-		       "screen=(%d,%d)-(%d,%d) %dx%d\n",
+-		       (unsigned)cli-&gt;id,
+-		       cli-&gt;app_id[0] ? cli-&gt;app_id : "?",
+-		       cli-&gt;x, cli-&gt;y, ww, wh,
+-		       a-&gt;x0, a-&gt;y0,
+-		       a-&gt;x1 &gt; a-&gt;x0 ? a-&gt;x1 - 1 : a-&gt;x0,
+-		       a-&gt;y1 &gt; a-&gt;y0 ? a-&gt;y1 - 1 : a-&gt;y0,
+-		       a-&gt;x1 - a-&gt;x0, a-&gt;y1 - a-&gt;y0);
+-		fflush(stdout);
+-	}
+-	blit_client_overlap(a-&gt;srv, a-&gt;cli, a-&gt;x0, a-&gt;y0, a-&gt;x1, a-&gt;y1);
++	return rect_make(a.x0 &lt; b.x0 ? a.x0 : b.x0,
++	                 a.y0 &lt; b.y0 ? a.y0 : b.y0,
++	                 a.x1 &gt; b.x1 ? a.x1 : b.x1,
++	                 a.y1 &gt; b.y1 ? a.y1 : b.y1);
+ }
+ 
++static struct rect rect_grow1(struct rect r, int max_x, int max_y)
++{
++	if (r.x0 &gt; 0)
++		r.x0--;
++	if (r.y0 &gt; 0)
++		r.y0--;
++	if (r.x1 &lt; max_x)
++		r.x1++;
++	if (r.y1 &lt; max_y)
++		r.y1++;
++	return r;
++}
++
++/* Clip to display; returns empty rect if nothing remains. */
++static struct rect rect_clip(const struct ServerState *srv, struct rect r)
++{
++	if (r.x0 &lt; 0)
++		r.x0 = 0;
++	if (r.y0 &lt; 0)
++		r.y0 = 0;
++	if (r.x1 &gt; (int)srv-&gt;display_w)
++		r.x1 = (int)srv-&gt;display_w;
++	if (r.y1 &gt; (int)srv-&gt;display_h)
++		r.y1 = (int)srv-&gt;display_h;
++	if (rect_empty(r))
++		return rect_make(0, 0, 0, 0);
++	return r;
++}
++
++/* Same ceil mapping as client_screen_bounds. */
++static struct rect rect_world_to_screen(const struct ServerState *srv,
++                                       struct rect world)
++{
++	int z = zoom_pct_of(srv);
++	struct rect s;
++
++	s.x0 = (world.x0 * z + 99) / 100 - srv-&gt;pan_x;
++	s.y0 = (world.y0 * z + 99) / 100 - srv-&gt;pan_y;
++	s.x1 = (world.x1 * z + 99) / 100 - srv-&gt;pan_x;
++	s.y1 = (world.y1 * z + 99) / 100 - srv-&gt;pan_y;
++	if (s.x1 &lt;= s.x0)
++		s.x1 = s.x0 + 1;
++	if (s.y1 &lt;= s.y0)
++		s.y1 = s.y0 + 1;
++	return s;
++}
++
++/* a \ b → up to 4 pieces in out[]; returns count. */
++static int rect_minus(struct rect a, struct rect b,
++                      struct rect *out, int out_max)
++{
++	int raw[4][4];
++	int n, i;
++
++	n = rect_subtract(a.x0, a.y0, a.x1, a.y1,
++	                  b.x0, b.y0, b.x1, b.y1, raw, out_max &lt; 4 ? out_max : 4);
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; n; i++)
++		out[i] = rect_make(raw[i][0], raw[i][1], raw[i][2], raw[i][3]);
++	return n;
++}
++
++static void rect_log(const char *tag, struct rect r)
++{
++	if (!bgce_comp_debug() || rect_empty(r))
++		return;
++	printf("[BGCE] move: %s [%d,%d)×[%d,%d) %dx%d\n",
++	       tag, r.x0, r.x1, r.y0, r.y1, r.x1 - r.x0, r.y1 - r.y0);
++	fflush(stdout);
++}
++
++/*
++ * Worker args: paint one screen rect (underlay stack or mover blit).
++ * Lifetime: stack of redraw_region until parallel join returns.
++ */
++struct move_paint_job {
++	struct ServerState *srv;
++	const struct Client *client; /* mover, or skip-id for underlay */
++	struct rect area;
++	int is_underlay; /* 1 = composite everyone except client */
++};
++
++static void move_paint_worker(void *arg)
++{
++	struct move_paint_job *job = arg;
++
++	bgce_comp_damage_log(job-&gt;is_underlay ? "underlay" : "mover",
++	                     job-&gt;area.x0, job-&gt;area.y0,
++	                     job-&gt;area.x1, job-&gt;area.y1, -1);
++	if (job-&gt;is_underlay)
++		composite_all_except(job-&gt;srv, job-&gt;client,
++		                     job-&gt;area.x0, job-&gt;area.y0,
++		                     job-&gt;area.x1, job-&gt;area.y1);
++	else
++		blit_client_overlap(job-&gt;srv, job-&gt;client,
++		                    job-&gt;area.x0, job-&gt;area.y0,
++		                    job-&gt;area.x1, job-&gt;area.y1);
++}
++
++/*
++ * Window move.  `c` is still at the OLD world position.
++ *
++ *   trail  = old_world \ new_world     (L-shape on a pure translate)
++ *   underlay each trail strip on screen (wallpaper + other windows)
++ *   blit mover on new_screen only
++ *   re-blit any windows above over old_screen ∪ new_screen
++ *
++ * Example: (1000,500) 200×200, left 1 → (999,500):
++ *   old_world  [1000,1200)×[500,700)
++ *   new_world  [999,1199)×[500,700)
++ *   trail      [1199,1200)×[500,700)   underlay 1×200
++ *   mover      [999,1199)×[500,700)    200×200  (no shared column)
++ */
+ void redraw_region(struct ServerState *srv, struct Client *c, int wdx, int wdy)
+ {
+-	struct Client moved;
+-	struct Client *p;
+-	int ox0, oy0, ox1, oy1;
+-	int nx0, ny0, nx1, ny1;
+-	int ux0, uy0, ux1, uy1;
+-	int bx0, by0, bx1, by1;
+-	int expose[8][4];
+-	int nexp;
+-	int i;
+-	int same_bounds;
+-	struct move_underlay_args uargs[2];
+-	struct move_blit_args bargs;
+-	void (*f0)(void *) = NULL, (*f1)(void *) = NULL, (*f2)(void *) = NULL;
+-	void *a0 = NULL, *a1 = NULL, *a2 = NULL;
++	struct Client at_new;
++	struct Client *above;
++	struct rect old_world, new_world;
++	struct rect old_screen, new_screen;
++	struct rect trail_world[MOVE_TRAIL_MAX];
++	struct rect trail_screen[MOVE_TRAIL_MAX];
++	struct move_paint_job underlay_job[2];
++	struct move_paint_job mover_job;
++	int width, height;
++	int n_trail, n_screen, i, j;
++	int z1x;
+

+commit c2fb92b
+parent <a href=commit-58f6e9f.html>58f6e9f</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-08T12:24:05-03:00
+
+    Startup logo, wallpaper fixes, zoom-sized windows, fast pan.
+
+    Print the BGCE ASCII mark at server start. Fix background config
+    parsing (any key order, trim values) and keep scaled wallpapers
+    stretched over the full virtual desktop.
+    
+    New clients get world geometry buffer/zoom so they look natural at
+    the current zoom without an ABI change. Pan shifts framebuffer
+    pixels and only composites the newly exposed edges; full redraw
+    remains for zoom.
+
+<a href=tree-c2fb92b.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>

+  * Request a shared memory buffer from the server.
+- * width/height are in virtual-desktop (world) pixels.
+- * Returns a mapped buffer pointer on success, or NULL on failure.

++ * places the window so it appears roughly that large on screen at the
++ * current zoom (world size = buffer / zoom). Returns a mapped buffer, or NULL.
+  */
+ void* bgce_get_buffer(int conn, struct BufferRequest req);

+ 
+ /* ----------------------------
+  * Cursor
+@@ -198,9 +214,17 @@ void redraw_region(struct ServerState* srv, struct Client c, int dx, int dy);
+

+-/** Full-scene recomposite (used after pan/zoom changes). */

+commit c6bfc91
+parent <a href=commit-42f8f3a.html>42f8f3a</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-16T12:21:57-03:00
+
+    Fix client disconnect race that could freeze the compositor.
+
+    Flush in-flight DRAW/MOVE before munmap so terminal shell exit
+    cannot tear down a buffer the paint path still uses.
+
+<a href=tree-c6bfc91.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/loop.c b/loop.c
+index 9badff7..626d700 100644
+--- a/loop.c
++++ b/loop.c
+@@ -268,54 +268,86 @@ void* client_thread(void* arg) {
+ 		}
+ 	}
+ 
+-	/* Stop any in-progress drag that targets this client (UAF otherwise). */
++	/*
++	 * Teardown order matters (async compositor):
++	 *
++	 *   1. Cancel drag targeting this client.
++	 *   2. Snapshot geometry / buffer for later munmap + erase.
++	 *   3. Unlink from the client list and clear focus so *new* jobs
++	 *      cannot find this client.
++	 *   4. Close the socket (no more MSG_DRAW from the peer).
++	 *   5. bgce_comp_flush() — wait until any in-flight DRAW/MOVE that
++	 *      already holds Client* + buffer finishes.  Munmap *before*
++	 *      this flush races the paint path and can SEGV the orchestrator
++	 *      (looks like a hard freeze: last frame stuck, no input).
++	 *   6. munmap / unlink shm / erase footprint / free.
++	 *
++	 * Terminals that exit the shell (e.g. `exit 1`) often disconnect with
++	 * DRAW jobs still queued — this race was easy to hit there.
++	 */
+ 	client_disconnected(client);
+ 
+-	if (client-&gt;buffer) {
+-		munmap(client-&gt;buffer, client-&gt;width * client-&gt;height * 4);
+-		client-&gt;buffer = NULL;
+-		bgce_buf_unlink(client-&gt;shm_name);
+-		client-&gt;shm_name[0] = '\0';
+-	}
++	{
++		uint32_t ww = client-&gt;world_w ? client-&gt;world_w : client-&gt;width;
++		uint32_t wh = client-&gt;world_h ? client-&gt;world_h : client-&gt;height;
++		uint32_t erase_x = client-&gt;x;
++		uint32_t erase_y = client-&gt;y;
++		void *buf = client-&gt;buffer;
++		size_t buf_bytes = 0;
++		char shm_name[64];
++		struct Client *prev = NULL;
++		struct Client *curr = server.clients;
++
++		if (buf &amp;&amp; client-&gt;width &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; client-&gt;height &gt; 0)
++			buf_bytes = (size_t)client-&gt;width * client-&gt;height * 4;
++		shm_name[0] = '\0';
++		if (client-&gt;shm_name[0]) {
++			strncpy(shm_name, client-&gt;shm_name, sizeof(shm_name) - 1);
++			shm_name[sizeof(shm_name) - 1] = '\0';
++		}
+ 
+-	/* Remove client from the linked list. */
+-	struct Client* prev = NULL;
+-	struct Client* curr = server.clients;
+-	while (curr) {
+-		if (curr == client) {
+-			if (prev)
+-				prev-&gt;next = curr-&gt;next;
+-			else
+-				server.clients = curr-&gt;next;
+-			break;
++		/* Unlink so find_client / pick_client stop seeing this node. */
++		while (curr) {
++			if (curr == client) {
++				if (prev)
++					prev-&gt;next = curr-&gt;next;
++				else
++					server.clients = curr-&gt;next;
++				break;
++			}
++			prev = curr;
++			curr = curr-&gt;next;
+ 		}
+-		prev = curr;
+-		curr = curr-&gt;next;
+-	}
++		client-&gt;next = NULL;
+ 
+-	if (server.focused_client == client) {
+-		/* Socket is already dead — do not write a focus-lost message. */
+-		server.focused_client = NULL;
+-	}
++		if (server.focused_client == client) {
++			/* Socket is already dead — do not write focus-lost. */
++			server.focused_client = NULL;
++		}
+ 
+-	close(client_fd);
+-	client-&gt;fd = -1;
++		close(client_fd);
++		client-&gt;fd = -1;
+ 
+-	/*
+-	 * Only repaint the closed window's screen rect from whatever is still
+-	 * in the stack.  Snapshot geometry into the job so paint is safe after
+-	 * free; flush so no in-flight DRAW still references this client.
+-	 */
+-	location_cache_remember_client(client);
+-	{
+-		uint32_t ww = client-&gt;world_w ? client-&gt;world_w : client-&gt;width;
+-		uint32_t wh = client-&gt;world_h ? client-&gt;world_h : client-&gt;height;
++		/* Drain paint that still references this Client and its buffer. */
++		bgce_comp_flush();
++
++		if (buf) {
++			munmap(buf, buf_bytes);
++			client-&gt;buffer = NULL;
++		}
++		if (shm_name[0]) {
++			bgce_buf_unlink(shm_name);
++			client-&gt;shm_name[0] = '\0';
++		}
+ 
+-		bgce_comp_submit_erase(client-&gt;x, client-&gt;y, ww, wh);
++		location_cache_remember_client(client);
++		/* Only the closed window's screen rect from remaining stack. */
++		bgce_comp_submit_erase(erase_x, erase_y, ww, wh);
+ 		bgce_comp_flush();
+ 	}
+ 
+-	printf("[BGCE] Client thread finished (fd=%d); server still running\n", client_fd);
++	printf("[BGCE] Client thread finished (fd=%d); server still running\n",
++	       client_fd);
+ 	free(client);
+ 	return NULL;
+ }
+</pre>

+<!DOCTYPE html>

+commit c77dec7
+parent <a href=commit-a2b2538.html>a2b2538</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-14T20:27:21-03:00
+
+    Coalesce pending MOVE/CURSOR/PAN jobs to avoid queue floods.
+
+    A fast drag enqueues a MOVE+CURSOR per pointer step and fills the 256
+    slot queue. Fold into an already-queued peer: MOVE keeps earliest old_*
+    and latest new_*; CURSOR keeps latest pos; PAN sums deltas. Only drop
+    when full and the job cannot coalesce.
+
+<a href=tree-c77dec7.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/compositor.c b/compositor.c
+index fd7c194..940e4ac 100644
+--- a/compositor.c
++++ b/compositor.c
+@@ -466,22 +466,148 @@ static void assign_job_id(struct comp_job *job)
+ 		job-&gt;job_id = next_job_id++;
+ }
+ 
++/*
++ * Fold high-frequency jobs into an already-queued peer so a fast drag does
++ * not enqueue hundreds of 1px MOVE + CURSOR steps (fills CAP → drops).
++ *
++ *   MOVE   same client → keep earliest old_*, set new_* to latest
++ *   CURSOR any         → latest screen position only
++ *   PAN    any         → accumulate sdx/sdy
++ *
++ * Must hold q_mu.  Returns 1 if absorbed (do not push a new slot).
++ */
++static int try_coalesce_locked(const struct comp_job *job)
++{
++	int i, n, idx;
++	struct comp_job *pending = NULL;
++
++	if (job-&gt;op != COMP_MOVE &amp;&amp; job-&gt;op != COMP_CURSOR &amp;&amp;
++	    job-&gt;op != COMP_PAN)
++		return 0;
++
++	n = q_count;
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; n; i++) {
++		idx = (q_head + i) % COMP_QUEUE_CAP;
++		if (queue[idx].op != job-&gt;op)
++			continue;
++		if (job-&gt;op == COMP_MOVE &amp;&amp;
++		    queue[idx].client_id != job-&gt;client_id)
++			continue;
++		pending = &amp;queue[idx];
++		/* keep scanning so we fold into the newest match */
++	}
++	if (!pending)
++		return 0;
++
++	if (job-&gt;op == COMP_MOVE) {
++		/* pending: A→B, job: B→C (or further) → one paint A→C */
++		pending-&gt;new_x = job-&gt;new_x;
++		pending-&gt;new_y = job-&gt;new_y;
++		if (bgce_debug) {
++			printf("[BGCE] comp: coalesce MOVE job=%llu client=%u "
++			       "(%d,%d)-&gt;(%d,%d) q=%d\n",
++			       (unsigned long long)pending-&gt;job_id,
++			       (unsigned)pending-&gt;client_id,
++			       pending-&gt;old_x, pending-&gt;old_y,
++			       pending-&gt;new_x, pending-&gt;new_y, q_count);
++			debug_fflush();
++		}
++	} else if (job-&gt;op == COMP_CURSOR) {
++		pending-&gt;cursor_x = job-&gt;cursor_x;
++		pending-&gt;cursor_y = job-&gt;cursor_y;
++		if (bgce_debug) {
++			printf("[BGCE] comp: coalesce CURSOR job=%llu "
++			       "screen=(%d,%d) q=%d\n",
++			       (unsigned long long)pending-&gt;job_id,
++			       pending-&gt;cursor_x, pending-&gt;cursor_y, q_count);
++			debug_fflush();
++		}
++	} else { /* COMP_PAN */
++		pending-&gt;sdx += job-&gt;sdx;
++		pending-&gt;sdy += job-&gt;sdy;
++		if (bgce_debug) {
++			printf("[BGCE] comp: coalesce PAN job=%llu d=(%d,%d) "
++			       "q=%d\n",
++			       (unsigned long long)pending-&gt;job_id,
++			       pending-&gt;sdx, pending-&gt;sdy, q_count);
++			debug_fflush();
++		}
++	}
++	return 1;
++}
++
++static void log_enqueue(const struct comp_job *job)
++{
++	struct Client *c = NULL;
++	const char *app = "";
++	uint32_t cx = 0, cy = 0, ww = 0, wh = 0;
++
++	if (!bgce_debug)
++		return;
++
++	if (job-&gt;client_id)
++		c = bgce_comp_find_client(job-&gt;client_id);
++	if (c) {
++		if (c-&gt;app_id[0])
++			app = c-&gt;app_id;
++		cx = c-&gt;x;
++		cy = c-&gt;y;
++		ww = c-&gt;world_w ? c-&gt;world_w : c-&gt;width;
++		wh = c-&gt;world_h ? c-&gt;world_h : c-&gt;height;
++	}
++	if (job-&gt;op == COMP_DRAW)
++		printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu DRAW client=%u "
++		       "app='%s' world=(%u,%u) %ux%u q=%d\n",
++		       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id,
++		       (unsigned)job-&gt;client_id, app, cx, cy, ww, wh,
++		       q_count);
++	else if (job-&gt;op == COMP_MOVE)
++		printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu MOVE client=%u "
++		       "app='%s' (%d,%d)-&gt;(%d,%d) q=%d\n",
++		       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id,
++		       (unsigned)job-&gt;client_id, app,
++		       job-&gt;old_x, job-&gt;old_y, job-&gt;new_x, job-&gt;new_y,
++		       q_count);
++	else if (job-&gt;op == COMP_PAN)
++		printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu PAN d=(%d,%d) q=%d\n",
++		       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id,
++		       job-&gt;sdx, job-&gt;sdy, q_count);
++	else if (job-&gt;op == COMP_CURSOR)
++		printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu CURSOR screen=(%d,%d) "
++		       "q=%d\n",
++		       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id,
++		       job-&gt;cursor_x, job-&gt;cursor_y, q_count);
++	else
++		printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu %s client=%u "
++		       "app='%s' q=%d\n",
++		       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id, op_name(job-&gt;op),
++		       (unsigned)job-&gt;client_id, app, q_count);
++	debug_fflush();
++}
++
+ /*
+  * Never block the producer (input) on a full queue — that freezes the mouse.
+- * Drop the new job if the queue is saturated (paint may lag; input stays live).
++ * Prefer coalescing MOVE/CURSOR/PAN; only drop if the queue is full and the
++ * job cannot fold into a peer.
+  */
+ static void enqueue(struct comp_job *job)
+ {
+ 	static int drop_log;
+ 
+-	assign_job_id(job);
+-
+ 	if (comp_sync) {
++		assign_job_id(job);
+ 		run_job(job);
+ 		return;
+ 	}
+ 
+ 	pthread_mutex_lock(&amp;q_mu);
++	if (try_coalesce_locked(job)) {
++		pthread_mutex_unlock(&amp;q_mu);
++		return;
++	}
++
++	assign_job_id(job);
++
+ 	if (q_count &gt;= COMP_QUEUE_CAP) {
+ 		pthread_mutex_unlock(&amp;q_mu);
+ 		if ((drop_log++ % 64) == 0) {
+@@ -495,50 +621,7 @@ static void enqueue(struct comp_job *job)
+ 	queue[q_tail] = *job;
+ 	q_tail = (q_tail + 1) % COMP_QUEUE_CAP;
+ 	q_count++;
+-	if (bgce_debug) {
+-		struct Client *c = NULL;
+-		const char *app = "";
+-		uint32_t cx = 0, cy = 0, ww = 0, wh = 0;
+-
+-		if (job-&gt;client_id)
+-			c = bgce_comp_find_client(job-&gt;client_id);
+-		if (c) {
+-			if (c-&gt;app_id[0])
+-				app = c-&gt;app_id;
+-			cx = c-&gt;x;
+-			cy = c-&gt;y;
+-			ww = c-&gt;world_w ? c-&gt;world_w : c-&gt;width;
+-			wh = c-&gt;world_h ? c-&gt;world_h : c-&gt;height;
+-		}
+-		if (job-&gt;op == COMP_DRAW)
+-			printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu DRAW client=%u "
+-			       "app='%s' world=(%u,%u) %ux%u q=%d\n",
+-			       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id,
+-			       (unsigned)job-&gt;client_id, app, cx, cy, ww, wh,
+-			       q_count);
+-		else if (job-&gt;op == COMP_MOVE)
+-			printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu MOVE client=%u "
+-			       "app='%s' (%d,%d)-&gt;(%d,%d) q=%d\n",
+-			       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id,
+-			       (unsigned)job-&gt;client_id, app,
+-			       job-&gt;old_x, job-&gt;old_y, job-&gt;new_x, job-&gt;new_y,
+-			       q_count);
+-		else if (job-&gt;op == COMP_PAN)
+-			printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu PAN d=(%d,%d) q=%d\n",
+-			       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id,
+-			       job-&gt;sdx, job-&gt;sdy, q_count);
+-		else if (job-&gt;op == COMP_CURSOR)
+-			printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu CURSOR screen=(%d,%d) "
+-			       "q=%d\n",
+-			       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id,
+-			       job-&gt;cursor_x, job-&gt;cursor_y, q_count);
+-		else
+-			printf("[BGCE] comp: enqueue job=%llu %s client=%u "
+-			       "app='%s' q=%d\n",
+-			       (unsigned long long)job-&gt;job_id, op_name(job-&gt;op),
+-			       (unsigned)job-&gt;client_id, app, q_count);
+-		debug_fflush();
+-	}
++	log_enqueue(job);
+ 	pthread_cond_signal(&amp;q_not_empty);
+ 	pthread_mutex_unlock(&amp;q_mu);
+ }
+diff --git a/compositor.h b/compositor.h
+index 8980922..906d4f1 100644
+--- a/compositor.h
++++ b/compositor.h
+@@ -11,6 +11,8 @@ struct Client;
+  * - Async mode: orchestrator pops jobs (DRAW/MOVE/PAN/CURSOR/…).
+  *   A pool of 3 blit workers runs fine-grained MOVE tasks FCFS.
+  *   Input never paints — it only enqueues (including mouse motion).
++ * - Pending MOVE (same client), CURSOR, and PAN jobs coalesce so a fast
++ *   drag paints one big step instead of flooding the queue.
+  * - Sync mode (headless): submit runs on the caller; parallel tasks serial.
+  *
+  * Debug: BGCE_DEBUG=1 — op names, enqueue/run/done, which worker took each
+</pre>

+ 
+ ### Input
+ - The server listens to keyboard and mouse events.
+-- Input is written to a FIFO that clients can read from.
+ - Focus determines which client receives input.
+ 
+ ### Drawing
+ - Each client owns its own off-screen buffer.
+ - The server composites buffers into the display based on Z-order.
+-- For now, **only one client** is supported.
+ 
+ ### Privileges
+ - BGCE must **run as a normal user** (no root, no setuid).
+@@ -49,8 +47,8 @@ void resizeBuffer(int width, int height); // Optional: resize client buffer
+ git clone &lt;repo-url&gt;
+ cd BGCE
+ make
+-./bgced   # Start server
+-./bgce-client  # Start test client
++./bgce   # Start server
++./client  # Start test client
+ ```
+ 
+ ## Goals

+
+commit cd04e4e
+parent <a href=commit-d9032c6.html>d9032c6</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-06-20T18:59:56-03:00
+
+    display: restored VT before DRM teardown to prevent frozen terminal
+
+    Moved release_vt() to the top of release_display() so KD_TEXT is
+    set before any DRM cleanup that could hang. Removed printf from
+    the signal handler to avoid async-signal-safety issues.
+
+<a href=tree-cd04e4e.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/display.c b/display.c
+index 75935f9..7829572 100644
+--- a/display.c
++++ b/display.c
+@@ -646,6 +646,10 @@ void redraw_from_resize(struct ServerState* srv, struct Client c, int dx, int dy
+ }
+ 
+ void release_display(void) {
++	/* Restore text mode first so the terminal is usable even if
++	 * the DRM teardown below hangs or crashes. */
++	release_vt();
++
+ 	if (cur_fb)
+ 		drmModeRmFB(drm_fd, cur_fb);
+ 
+@@ -681,8 +685,6 @@ void release_display(void) {
+ 	if (encoder)
+ 		drmModeFreeEncoder(encoder);
+ 
+-	release_vt();
+-
+ 	close(drm_fd);
+ 	printf("[BGCE] Display released.\n");
+ }
+diff --git a/server.c b/server.c
+index a629947..6e7a40d 100644
+--- a/server.c
++++ b/server.c
+@@ -25,7 +25,7 @@ static void ensure_dir(const char *path) {
+ }
+ 
+ static void cleanup_and_exit(int sig) {
+-	printf("[BGCE] Caught signal %d, cleaning up\n", sig);
++	(void)sig;
+ 	release_display();
+ 	_exit(0);
+ }
+</pre>

+parent <a href=commit-4b05df2.html>4b05df2</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-06-20T18:52:02-03:00
+
+    display: switched VT to KD_GRAPHICS to suppress keystroke echo
+
+    Added setup_vt_handling() to set KD_GRAPHICS on the active tty during
+    init, and restore KD_TEXT in release_display(). Added SIGINT/SIGTERM
+    handler in server.c to ensure cleanup runs on termination.
+
+<a href=tree-d9032c6.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/display.c b/display.c
+index 4c3326a..75935f9 100644
+--- a/display.c
++++ b/display.c
+@@ -21,6 +21,8 @@
+ #include "server.h"
+ #include &lt;errno.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;fcntl.h&gt;
++#include &lt;linux/kd.h&gt;
++#include &lt;linux/vt.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;stdbool.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;stdint.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;stdio.h&gt;
+@@ -57,6 +59,8 @@
+ 
+ extern struct ServerState server;
+ 
++static int vt_fd = -1;
++
+ int drm_fd = -1;
+ uint32_t conn_id = 0;
+ uint32_t cur_fb = 0;
+@@ -127,6 +131,43 @@ static void draw_cursor(uint8_t* buf, uint32_t stride, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {
+ 	}
+ }
+ 
++int setup_vt_handling(void) {
++	/* Try the current tty first, then fall back to /dev/tty0 */
++	vt_fd = open("/dev/tty", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
++	if (vt_fd &lt; 0)
++		vt_fd = open("/dev/tty0", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
++	if (vt_fd &lt; 0) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: cannot open tty: %s "
++		        "(keystrokes will echo on the console)\n",
++		        strerror(errno));
++		return -1;
++	}
++
++	if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDSETMODE, KD_GRAPHICS) &lt; 0) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDSETMODE KD_GRAPHICS failed: %s "
++		        "(keystrokes will echo on the console)\n",
++		        strerror(errno));
++		close(vt_fd);
++		vt_fd = -1;
++		return -1;
++	}
++
++	printf("[BGCE] VT: switched to KD_GRAPHICS mode\n");
++	return 0;
++}
++
++static void release_vt(void) {
++	if (vt_fd &lt; 0)
++		return;
++	if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDSETMODE, KD_TEXT) &lt; 0)
++		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDSETMODE KD_TEXT failed: %s\n",
++		        strerror(errno));
++	else
++		printf("[BGCE] VT: restored KD_TEXT mode\n");
++	close(vt_fd);
++	vt_fd = -1;
++}
++
+ int init_display() {
+ 	uint32_t crtc_id = 0;
+ 	drmModeModeInfo chosen_mode;
+@@ -147,10 +188,7 @@ int init_display() {
+ 	}
+ 	server.drm_fd = drm_fd;
+ 
+-	// if (setup_vt_handling() &lt; 0) {
+-	//	close(server-&gt;drm_fd);
+-	//	return -1;
+-	// }
++	setup_vt_handling();
+ 
+ 	resources = drmModeGetResources(drm_fd);
+ 	if (!resources) {
+@@ -643,6 +681,8 @@ void release_display(void) {
+ 	if (encoder)
+ 		drmModeFreeEncoder(encoder);
+ 
++	release_vt();
++
+ 	close(drm_fd);
+ 	printf("[BGCE] Display released.\n");
+ }
+diff --git a/server.c b/server.c
+index 5f3b974..a629947 100644
+--- a/server.c
++++ b/server.c
+@@ -24,6 +24,12 @@ static void ensure_dir(const char *path) {
+ 	mkdir(path, 0755);
+ }
+ 
++static void cleanup_and_exit(int sig) {
++	printf("[BGCE] Caught signal %d, cleaning up\n", sig);
++	release_display();
++	_exit(0);
++}
++
+ static void setup_log_file(void) {
+ 	const char *xdg = getenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME");
+ 	const char *home = getenv("HOME");
+@@ -68,6 +74,10 @@ int main(void) {
+ 	/* Auto-reap child processes so command shortcuts don't leave zombies */
+ 	signal(SIGCHLD, SIG_IGN);
+ 
++	/* Ensure VT is restored on termination signals */
++	signal(SIGINT, cleanup_and_exit);
++	signal(SIGTERM, cleanup_and_exit);
++
+ 	memset(&amp;server, 0, sizeof(struct ServerState));
+ 	server.drm_fd = -1;
+ 	server.framebuffer = NULL;
+</pre>

diff --git a/www/commit-ddea799.html b/www/commit-ddea799.html
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b69db8a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/www/commit-ddea799.html
@@ -0,0 +1,157 @@
+<!DOCTYPE html>
+<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
+<title>bgce ddea799</title>
+<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
+<link rel=icon href=data:,>

+<pre>
+<a href=index.html>bgce</a> / <b>commit</b>

+commit ddea799
+parent <a href=commit-0d63547.html>0d63547</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-08T14:06:34-03:00
+
+    Detach VT keyboard and shortcut children from the console tty.
+
+    KD_GRAPHICS alone still fed keys to the line discipline. Set KDSKBMODE
+    K_OFF (restored on exit) so only /dev/input reaches clients, and point
+    shortcut children at /dev/null after setsid so new apps are not born on
+    the controlling terminal.
+
+<a href=tree-ddea799.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/display.c b/display.c
+index 19b0731..3bb1b53 100644
+--- a/display.c
++++ b/display.c
+@@ -24,6 +24,12 @@ extern struct ServerState server;
+ extern struct config config;
+ 
+ static int vt_fd = -1;
++/* Previous KDSKBMODE so we can restore on exit (KDGKBMODE uses long). */
++static long vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
++#ifndef K_OFF
++/* Disabled keyboard → console (Linux ≥ 2.6.39). */
++#define K_OFF 0x04
++#endif
+ 
+ #if CURSOR_WIDTH != 32 || CURSOR_HEIGHT != 32
+ #error "software cursor blit assumes CURSOR_WIDTH/HEIGHT == 32"
+@@ -482,38 +488,72 @@ void set_cursor_type(enum BGCECursorType type)
+ 
+ 
+ int setup_vt_handling(void) {
+-	/* Try the current tty first, then fall back to /dev/tty0 */
++	/*
++	 * KD_GRAPHICS only stops the *console driver drawing* text.
++	 * Keys still go to the VT line discipline unless we also disable
++	 * keyboard mode (K_OFF).  Without that, getty/shell/new apps on the
++	 * same tty still see keystrokes while bgce reads /dev/input.
++	 */
+ 	vt_fd = open("/dev/tty", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
+ 	if (vt_fd &lt; 0)
+ 		vt_fd = open("/dev/tty0", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
+ 	if (vt_fd &lt; 0) {
+ 		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: cannot open tty: %s "
+-		        "(keystrokes will echo on the console)\n",
++		        "(keystrokes may still go to the console)\n",
+ 		        strerror(errno));
+ 		return -1;
+ 	}
+ 
++	vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
++	if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDGKBMODE, &amp;vt_saved_kbmode) &lt; 0) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDGKBMODE failed: %s\n",
++		        strerror(errno));
++		vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
++	}
++
+ 	if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDSETMODE, KD_GRAPHICS) &lt; 0) {
+ 		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDSETMODE KD_GRAPHICS failed: %s "
+-		        "(keystrokes will echo on the console)\n",
++		        "(keystrokes may still go to the console)\n",
+ 		        strerror(errno));
+ 		close(vt_fd);
+ 		vt_fd = -1;
++		vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
+ 		return -1;
+ 	}
+ 
+-	printf("[BGCE] VT: switched to KD_GRAPHICS mode\n");
++	/*
++	 * Silence the VT keyboard: no more cooked input / Ctrl+C / echo for
++	 * processes on this console.  bgce keeps using /dev/input/event*.
++	 */
++	if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDSKBMODE, (long)K_OFF) &lt; 0) {
++		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDSKBMODE K_OFF failed: %s "
++		        "(keys may still reach the tty)\n",
++		        strerror(errno));
++	} else {
++		printf("[BGCE] VT: KD_GRAPHICS + keyboard off "
++		       "(input via /dev/input only)\n");
++	}
++
+ 	return 0;
+ }
+ 
+ void release_vt(void) {
+ 	if (vt_fd &lt; 0)
+ 		return;
++
++	if (vt_saved_kbmode &gt;= 0) {
++		if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDSKBMODE, vt_saved_kbmode) &lt; 0)
++			fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: restore KDSKBMODE failed: %s\n",
++			        strerror(errno));
++		vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
++	}
++
+ 	if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDSETMODE, KD_TEXT) &lt; 0)
+ 		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDSETMODE KD_TEXT failed: %s\n",
+ 		        strerror(errno));
+ 	else
+-		printf("[BGCE] VT: restored KD_TEXT mode\n");
++		printf("[BGCE] VT: restored KD_TEXT + keyboard mode\n");
++
+ 	close(vt_fd);
+ 	vt_fd = -1;
+ }
+diff --git a/input.c b/input.c
+index 3f7649d..5a4a49c 100644
+--- a/input.c
++++ b/input.c
+@@ -499,16 +499,23 @@ static int handle_input_event(struct input_event ev, size_t dev_idx) {
+ 			} else if (sc-&gt;type == SHORTCUT_COMMAND) {
+ 				pid_t pid = fork();
+ 				if (pid == 0) {
++					int devnull;
+ 					/*
+-					 * Leave bgce's process group / session.  Otherwise a
+-					 * terminal Ctrl+C delivers SIGINT to every shortcut
+-					 * child as well as the server (kernel process-group
+-					 * broadcast), while bgce only meant to forward a
+-					 * synthetic Ctrl+C to the focused client.
++					 * Detach from bgce's session/tty so the child is not
++					 * a console job: no process-group SIGINT with the
++					 * server, and no stdin/stdout bound to the VT (apps
++					 * would otherwise treat the tty as their terminal).
+ 					 */
+ 					if (setsid() &lt; 0)
+-						/* still try to run; better than _exit */
+ 						(void)setpgid(0, 0);
++					devnull = open("/dev/null", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
++					if (devnull &gt;= 0) {
++						dup2(devnull, STDIN_FILENO);
++						dup2(devnull, STDOUT_FILENO);
++						dup2(devnull, STDERR_FILENO);
++						if (devnull &gt; STDERR_FILENO)
++							close(devnull);
++					}
+ 					signal(SIGINT, SIG_DFL);
+ 					signal(SIGTERM, SIG_DFL);
+ 					execl("/bin/sh", "sh", "-c", sc-&gt;value, (char *)NULL);
+</pre>

+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2025-12-15T20:49:02-03:00

+    updated readme

+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
+index c905cca..6437a00 100644
+--- a/README.md
++++ b/README.md
+@@ -1,5 +1,21 @@
+ # BGCE: Brian's Graphical Computer Environment
+ 
++```
++	┌────────────────────────────────────┐
++	│ BGCE.                              │
++	│     |\                             │
++	│      ^                             │
++	│                   ┌───────┐        │
++	│      ┌───────┐    │       │        │
++	│      │       │    │       │        │
++	│      │       │    │       │        │
++	│      │       │    │       │        │
++	│      └───────┘    └───────┘        │
++	│                                    │
++	└────────────────────────────────────┘
++```
++
++
+ BGCE is a minimal graphical environment for Linux written in C. It acts as a bare-bones window system, similar in concept to Xorg or Wayland, but much simpler and designed to run **without root privileges**.
+ 
+ ## Overview
+@@ -23,22 +39,38 @@ Buffer* getBuffer(int width, int height); // Returns a pointer to the client’s
+ void draw(); // Requests server to draw the client buffer
+ ```
+ 
++I posted a video on my blog:
++
++[Post](https://blog.terminal.pink/posts/bgce.html)
++
++
++### Goals
++
++- Minimal, understandable graphics stack in C
++- No external dependencies (no OpenGL, no X11, no Wayland)
++- Educational reference for framebuffer-based compositing and IPC
++
++
+ ### Input
+ - The server listens to keyboard and mouse events.
+ - Focus determines which client receives input.
+ 
++
+ ### Drawing
+ - Each client owns its own off-screen buffer.
+ - The server composites buffers into the display based on Z-order.
+ 
++
+ ### Privileges
+ - BGCE must **run as a normal user** (no root, no setuid).
+-- The user should be in the **video** group to access `/dev/fb0` (framebuffer device).
++- The user should be in the **video** group to access `/dev/dri/card1` (framebuffer device).
++
+ 
+ ### Event Loop
+ - Communication is **blocking** for events and **asynchronous** for draw requests.
+ - Future versions will include multiple clients and input focus management.
+ 
++
+ ## Build Instructions
+ 
+ ```bash
+@@ -46,14 +78,26 @@ git clone &lt;repo-url&gt;
+ cd BGCE
+ make all client
+ ./bgce   # Start server
++# Go to a different tty
+ ./client  # Start test client
+ ```
+ 
+-## Goals
+ 
+-- Minimal, understandable graphics stack in C
+-- No external dependencies (no OpenGL, no X11, no Wayland)
+-- Educational reference for framebuffer-based compositing and IPC
++## Developing client applications
++
++BGCE clients should write directly to the buffer
++and call draw(), so the server will draw it to the
++screen. When users resize the window an event is
++sent to the client, applications then should adjust
++its content and call `draw()`.
++
++You are free to choose any libraries to help with
++drawing graphical elements. To be honest I don't
++know if the most common ones can directly handle
++buffers. So I am creating a toolkit:
++[BGTK](https://terminal.pink/bgtk/index.html), check it
++out if you want.
++
+ 
+ ## License
+ 
+</pre>

++# writes headless_00_bg.png … headless_08_location_restored.png
+ ```
+ 
+ API (see `mock.h`): `bgce_mock_init`, `bgce_mock_add_client`, `bgce_mock_draw`,
+@@ -49,7 +49,7 @@ kernel headers. Real `bgce` still requires Linux.
+ [X] Implement taking screenshots

+-[ ] Implement a cache file to memorize the last location of clients, in order to reopen them on the same place

+ 
+ ### Protocol features

+@@ -59,6 +59,14 @@ kernel headers. Real `bgce` still requires Linux.

++  - [X] headless location-cache restore
++
++### Location cache
++- File: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/bgce/windows.cache` or `~/.cache/bgce/windows.cache`
++- Format: `app_id x y` (world pixels), one entry per line
++- Identity: Linux `SO_PEERCRED` + `/proc/pid/comm` (fallback `"client"`)
++- Restore on first buffer request; save on move end, MSG_MOVE, and disconnect
++- Same binary name shares one slot (last place wins)
+ 
+ ### Zoom / pan controls
+ - **Alt + scroll**: zoom in/out toward the cursor (range 0.5×–4.0×)

+@@ -0,0 +1,256 @@
++/*
++ * Persist last window positions per app id under the user cache dir:
++ *   $XDG_CACHE_HOME/bgce/windows.cache
++ *   or ~/.cache/bgce/windows.cache
++ *
++ * File format (one entry per line):
++ *   app_id x y
++ */
++
++#define _GNU_SOURCE
++#include "location_cache.h"
++#include "server.h"
++
++#include &lt;errno.h&gt;
++#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;
++#include &lt;stdlib.h&gt;
++#include &lt;string.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/socket.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/stat.h&gt;
++#include &lt;unistd.h&gt;
++
++#ifndef SO_PEERCRED
++/* Non-Linux: identification falls back to "client". */
++#endif
++
++#define LOC_CACHE_MAX 64
++#define LOC_ID_MAX 64
++
++struct loc_entry {
++	char id[LOC_ID_MAX];
++	uint32_t x;
++	uint32_t y;
++	int used;
++};
++
++static struct loc_entry entries[LOC_CACHE_MAX];
++static int entries_loaded;
++
++static int cache_dir(char *buf, size_t buflen)
++{
++	const char *xdg = getenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME");
++	const char *home = getenv("HOME");
++	int n;
++

++		n = snprintf(buf, buflen, "%s/bgce", xdg);
++	else if (home &amp;&amp; home[0])
++		n = snprintf(buf, buflen, "%s/.cache/bgce", home);
++	else
++		return -1;
++	if (n &lt; 0 || (size_t)n &gt;= buflen)
++		return -1;
++	return 0;
++}
++
++static int cache_path(char *buf, size_t buflen)
++{
++	char dir[512];
++
++	if (cache_dir(dir, sizeof(dir)) &lt; 0)
++		return -1;
++	if (snprintf(buf, buflen, "%s/windows.cache", dir) &gt;= (int)buflen)
++		return -1;
++	return 0;
++}
++
++static void ensure_cache_dir(void)
++{
++	char dir[512];
++	char parent[512];
++	const char *home;
++	const char *xdg;
++
++	if (cache_dir(dir, sizeof(dir)) &lt; 0)
++		return;
++
++	xdg = getenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME");
++	home = getenv("HOME");
++	if (xdg &amp;&amp; xdg[0] == '/') {
++		mkdir(xdg, 0700);
++	} else if (home &amp;&amp; home[0]) {
++		snprintf(parent, sizeof(parent), "%s/.cache", home);
++		mkdir(parent, 0700);
++	}
++	mkdir(dir, 0700);
++}
++
++void location_cache_load(void)
++{
++	char path[512];
++	FILE *f;
++	char line[256];
++	int i;
++
++	memset(entries, 0, sizeof(entries));
++	entries_loaded = 1;
++
++	if (cache_path(path, sizeof(path)) &lt; 0)
++		return;
++	f = fopen(path, "r");
++	if (!f)
++		return;
++
++	i = 0;
++	while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f) &amp;&amp; i &lt; LOC_CACHE_MAX) {
++		char id[LOC_ID_MAX];
++		unsigned int x, y;
++
++		if (line[0] == '#' || line[0] == '\n')
++			continue;
++		if (sscanf(line, "%63s %u %u", id, &amp;x, &amp;y) != 3)
++			continue;
++		strncpy(entries[i].id, id, sizeof(entries[i].id) - 1);
++		entries[i].x = x;
++		entries[i].y = y;
++		entries[i].used = 1;
++		i++;
++	}
++	fclose(f);
++	printf("[BGCE] location cache: loaded %d entr%s from %s\n",
++	       i, i == 1 ? "y" : "ies", path);
++}
++
++void location_cache_save(void)
++{
++	char path[512];
++	FILE *f;
++	int i, n = 0;
++
++	if (!entries_loaded)
++		return;
++	ensure_cache_dir();
++	if (cache_path(path, sizeof(path)) &lt; 0)
++		return;
++
++	f = fopen(path, "w");
++	if (!f) {
++		perror("[BGCE] location cache write");
++		return;
++	}
++	fprintf(f, "# BGCE window locations: app_id x y (world pixels)\n");
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; LOC_CACHE_MAX; i++) {
++		if (!entries[i].used)
++			continue;
++		fprintf(f, "%s %u %u\n", entries[i].id, entries[i].x,
++		        entries[i].y);
++		n++;
++	}
++	fclose(f);
++	printf("[BGCE] location cache: saved %d entr%s to %s\n",
++	       n, n == 1 ? "y" : "ies", path);
++}
++
++int location_cache_lookup(const char *app_id, uint32_t *x, uint32_t *y)
++{
++	int i;
++
++	if (!app_id || !app_id[0] || !entries_loaded)
++		return 0;
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; LOC_CACHE_MAX; i++) {
++		if (entries[i].used &amp;&amp; strcmp(entries[i].id, app_id) == 0) {
++			if (x)
++				*x = entries[i].x;
++			if (y)
++				*y = entries[i].y;
++			return 1;
++		}
++	}
++	return 0;
++}
++
++void location_cache_store(const char *app_id, uint32_t x, uint32_t y)
++{
++	int i;
++	int free_slot = -1;
++
++	if (!app_id || !app_id[0])
++		return;
++	if (!entries_loaded)
++		location_cache_load();
++
++	for (i = 0; i &lt; LOC_CACHE_MAX; i++) {
++		if (entries[i].used &amp;&amp; strcmp(entries[i].id, app_id) == 0) {
++			entries[i].x = x;
++			entries[i].y = y;
++			return;
++		}
++		if (!entries[i].used &amp;&amp; free_slot &lt; 0)
++			free_slot = i;
++	}
++	if (free_slot &lt; 0)
++		free_slot = 0; /* overwrite first if full */
++	strncpy(entries[free_slot].id, app_id, sizeof(entries[free_slot].id) - 1);
++	entries[free_slot].id[sizeof(entries[free_slot].id) - 1] = '\0';
++	entries[free_slot].x = x;
++	entries[free_slot].y = y;
++	entries[free_slot].used = 1;
++}
++
++void location_cache_identify_client(struct Client *client, int sock_fd)
++{
++	if (!client)

++#ifdef SO_PEERCRED
++	{

++		memset(&amp;cred, 0, sizeof(cred));

++		    cred.pid &gt; 0) {
++			client-&gt;pid = cred.pid;
++			snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/proc/%d/comm", (int)cred.pid);

++						        '\0';
++					}
++				}
++				fclose(f);
++			}
++		}
++	}
++#else
++	(void)sock_fd;
++#endif

++	       (int)client-&gt;pid);
++}

+commit e30d1b3
+parent <a href=commit-2b4ba9a.html>2b4ba9a</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-06-19T17:02:10-03:00
+
+    Added default cache log file, fixed DRM includes, improved input detection, and normalized logs
+
+    - Added default log file at $XDG_CACHE_HOME/bgce/bgce.log (or ~/.cache/bgce/bgce.log)
+    - Redirected stdout/stderr so all [BGCE] output is captured
+    - Added __has_include guards for &lt;drm/drm_mode.h&gt; and &lt;libdrm/drm_mode.h&gt;
+    - Improved init_input() with EV_ABS support, key/button qualification, and permission error hints
+    - Prefixed all remaining bare perror/printf/fprintf with [BGCE]
+    - Updated Makefile test targets with proper defaults
+    - Fixed hardcoded /dev/dri/card1 and added missing cur_w/cur_h
+
+<a href=tree-e30d1b3.html>tree</a>
+

+ 
+ BGCE supports configuration for the background through a config file. By default, it looks for `~/.config/bgce.conf`.
+ 
++## Logging
++
++All server messages are written to a default log file:
++
++- `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/bgce/bgce.log` (if `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is set)
++- otherwise `~/.cache/bgce/bgce.log`
++
++The path is printed to the terminal you used to start `bgce` so you know where to look (`tail -f` it, etc.). All `[BGCE]` output after that point goes into the log file.
++
+ 
+ ### Config File Format
+ 
+diff --git a/config.c b/config.c

++++ b/config.c

+ 		int img_width, img_height, img_channels;
+ 		unsigned char* img_data = stbi_load(config-&gt;path, &amp;img_width, &amp;img_height, &amp;img_channels, 4);

++		return;

++static void setup_log_file(void) {
++	const char *xdg = getenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME");
++	const char *home = getenv("HOME");
++	char dir[512];

++	if (xdg &amp;&amp; xdg[0]) {

++		ensure_dir(dotcache);

++	} else {

++	}
++
++	char log_path[512];
++	snprintf(log_path, sizeof(log_path), "%s/bgce.log", dir);
++
++	int fd = open(log_path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND, 0600);
++	if (fd &lt; 0)
++		return;
++
++	/* Tell the user (on their original terminal) where logs are going */
++	dprintf(STDERR_FILENO, "[BGCE] Logging to %s\n", log_path);

+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
+index 7a41137..a3c727b 100644
+--- a/README.md
++++ b/README.md
+@@ -13,7 +13,7 @@ The server maintains:
+ - A **real display buffer** (the VGA framebuffer)
+ - A **per-client off-screen buffer**
+ - Basic **input handling** (keyboard + mouse)
+-- **IPC** using UNIX domain sockets (for commands) and FIFOs (for input events)
++- **IPC** using UNIX domain sockets for commands and input events
+ 
+ The client communicates with the server via a shared library exposing these APIs:
+ 
+diff --git a/bgce-client-handler.c b/bgce-client-handler.c
+new file mode 100644
+index 0000000..f556fbe
+--- /dev/null
++++ b/bgce-client-handler.c
+@@ -0,0 +1,99 @@
++#include "bgce.h"
++#include "bgce_shared.h"
++
++#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;
++#include &lt;stdlib.h&gt;
++#include &lt;string.h&gt;
++#include &lt;unistd.h&gt;
++#include &lt;fcntl.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/mman.h&gt;
++#include &lt;sys/stat.h&gt;
++#include &lt;time.h&gt;
++
++/* Handle a single connected client */
++void handle_client(int client_fd, ServerState *server)
++{
++	Client client = {0};
++	client.fd = client_fd;
++
++	printf("[BGCE] Client connected (fd=%d)\n", client_fd);
++
++	while (1) {
++		BGCEMessage msg;
++		ssize_t rc = bgce_recv_msg(client_fd, &amp;msg);
++		if (rc &lt;= 0) {
++			printf("[BGCE] Client disconnected (fd=%d)\n", client_fd);
++			break;
++		}
++
++		switch (msg.type) {
++		case MSG_GET_SERVER_INFO: {
++			ServerInfo info = {
++				.width = server-&gt;width,
++				.height = server-&gt;height,
++				.color_depth = server-&gt;color_depth
++			};
++			bgce_send_data(client_fd, &amp;info, sizeof(info));
++			break;
++		}
++
++		case MSG_GET_BUFFER: {
++			if (msg.length &lt; sizeof(ClientBufferRequest)) {
++				fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] Invalid buffer request size\n");
++				break;
++			}
++			ClientBufferRequest req;
++			memcpy(&amp;req, msg.data, sizeof(req));
++
++			snprintf(client.shm_name, sizeof(client.shm_name),
++				 "/bgce_buf_%d_%ld", getpid(), time(NULL));
++
++			int shm_fd = shm_open(client.shm_name, O_CREAT | O_RDWR, 0600);
++			if (shm_fd &lt; 0) {
++				perror("shm_open");
++				break;
++			}
++
++			size_t buf_size = req.width * req.height * 3;
++			if (ftruncate(shm_fd, buf_size) &lt; 0) {
++				perror("ftruncate");
++				close(shm_fd);
++				break;
++			}
++
++			client.buffer = mmap(NULL, buf_size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_SHARED, shm_fd, 0);
++			client.width = req.width;
++			client.height = req.height;
++			close(shm_fd);
++
++			ClientBufferReply reply = {0};
++			strncpy(reply.shm_name, client.shm_name, sizeof(reply.shm_name));
++			reply.width = req.width;
++			reply.height = req.height;
++			bgce_send_data(client_fd, &amp;reply, sizeof(reply));
++			break;
++		}
++
++		case MSG_DRAW: {
++			if (!client.buffer) {
++				fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] Client has no buffer!\n");
++				break;
++			}
++			printf("[BGCE] Drawing from client %d\n", client_fd);
++			bgce_blit_to_framebuffer(server, &amp;client);
++			break;
++		}
++
++		default:
++			fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] Unknown message type %d\n", msg.type);
++			break;
++		}
++	}
++
++	if (client.buffer) {
++		munmap(client.buffer, client.width * client.height * 3);
++		shm_unlink(client.shm_name);
++	}
++	close(client_fd);
++}
++
+</pre>

++&lt;!DOCTYPE html&gt;
++&lt;meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" /&gt;
++&lt;title&gt;BGCE&lt;/title&gt;
++&lt;meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"&gt;
++&lt;link rel=icon href=data:,&gt;
++&lt;link rel=alternate type="application/rss+xml" title=log href=feed.xml /&gt;
++&lt;style&gt;pre{width:52ch;margin:2ch auto}a{color:#ff00ff}&lt;/style&gt;
++&lt;pre&gt;
++	┌────────────────────────┐
++	│                        │
++	│ BGCE.                  │
++	│     |\                 │
++	│                        │
++	└────────────────────────┘
++
++&lt;i&gt;&lt;b&gt;BGCE: Brian's Graphical Computer Environment&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/i&gt;
++
++BGCE is a minimal graphical environment for Linux
++written in C. It acts as a bare-bones window system
++similar to Xorg or Wayland, but much simpler and
++designed to run &lt;b&gt;without root privileges&lt;/b&gt;.
++
++
++&lt;b&gt;Overview&lt;/b&gt;
++
++The system is split into two components:
++
++- &lt;b&gt;Server:&lt;/b&gt; Manages video buffer, input events, and
++  window stacking.
++- &lt;b&gt;Client:&lt;/b&gt; Applications that render to their own
++  buffers and request drawing through the server.
++
++
++&lt;b&gt;Build Instructions&lt;/b&gt;
++
++	git clone https://terminal.pink/bgce
++	cd bgce
++	make
++	./bgce   # Start server
++	./client  # Start test client
++
++
++&lt;b&gt;Goals&lt;/b&gt;
++
++- Minimal, understandable graphics stack in C
++- No external dependencies like OpenGL, X11 etc
++- Educational reference for framebuffer-based
++  compositing and IPC
++
++
++&lt;b&gt;License&lt;/b&gt;
++
++MIT License
++&lt;/pre&gt;
+</pre>

+diff --git a/shared.c b/shared.c
+deleted file mode 100644
+index a5179dc..0000000
+--- a/shared.c
++++ /dev/null
+@@ -1,82 +0,0 @@
+-#define _XOPEN_SOURCE 700
+-
+-#include "bgce.h"
+-#include "shared.h"
+-
+-#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;
+-#include &lt;stdlib.h&gt;
+-#include &lt;string.h&gt;
+-#include &lt;errno.h&gt;
+-#include &lt;sys/mman.h&gt;
+-#include &lt;fcntl.h&gt;
+-#include &lt;unistd.h&gt;
+-
+-/* ============================================================
+- *  LOW-LEVEL SOCKET UTILITIES
+- * ============================================================ */
+-
+-/* Write exactly 'size' bytes */
+-ssize_t bgce_send_data(int fd, const void *data, size_t size)
+-{
+-    const char *buf = data;
+-    size_t total = 0;
+-    while (total &lt; size) {
+-        ssize_t n = write(fd, buf + total, size - total);
+-        if (n &lt; 0) {
+-            if (errno == EINTR)
+-                continue;
+-            perror("write");
+-            return -1;
+-        }
+-        if (n == 0)
+-            break;
+-        total += n;
+-    }
+-    return (ssize_t)total;
+-}
+-
+-/* Read exactly 'size' bytes */
+-ssize_t bgce_recv_data(int fd, void *data, size_t size)
+-{
+-    char *buf = data;
+-    size_t total = 0;
+-    while (total &lt; size) {
+-        ssize_t n = read(fd, buf + total, size - total);
+-        if (n &lt; 0) {
+-            if (errno == EINTR)
+-                continue;
+-            perror("read");
+-            return -1;
+-        }
+-        if (n == 0)
+-            break;
+-        total += n;
+-    }
+-    return (ssize_t)total;
+-}
+-
+-/* ============================================================
+- *  MESSAGE HELPERS
+- * ============================================================ */
+-
+-ssize_t bgce_send_msg(int fd, const struct BGCEMessage *msg)
+-{
+-    size_t len = sizeof(msg-&gt;type) + sizeof(msg-&gt;length) + msg-&gt;length;
+-    return bgce_send_data(fd, msg, len);
+-}
+-
+-ssize_t bgce_recv_msg(int fd, struct BGCEMessage *msg)
+-{
+-    ssize_t n = bgce_recv_data(fd, msg, sizeof(uint32_t) * 2);
+-    if (n &lt;= 0)
+-        return n;
+-
+-    if (msg-&gt;length &gt; 0) {
+-        ssize_t d = bgce_recv_data(fd, msg-&gt;data, msg-&gt;length);
+-        if (d &lt; 0)
+-            return -1;
+-        n += d;
+-    }
+-    return n;
+-}
+-

+-/* ----------------------------
+- * Shared Utilities
+- * ---------------------------- */
+-
+-/**
+- * Send raw data over a socket (blocking until all bytes sent).
+- * Returns number of bytes written, or -1 on error.
+- */
+-ssize_t bgce_send_data(int fd, const void *data, size_t size);
+-
+-/**
+- * Receive raw data over a socket (blocking until full message read).
+- * Returns number of bytes read, or -1 on error.
+- */
+-ssize_t bgce_recv_data(int fd, void *data, size_t size);
+-
+-/**
+- * Send a structured BGCE message.
+- * Returns total bytes sent, or -1 on error.
+- */
+-ssize_t bgce_send_msg(int fd, const struct BGCEMessage *msg);
+-
+-/**
+- * Receive a structured BGCE message.
+- * Returns total bytes read, or -1 on error.
+- */
+-ssize_t bgce_recv_msg(int fd, struct BGCEMessage *msg);
+-
+-#endif /* BGCE_SHARED_H */

+commit f6362a6
+parent <a href=commit-e5ff961.html>e5ff961</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-06T16:06:57-03:00
+
+    Keep server alive on client crash; timestamp log lines.
+
+    Ignore SIGPIPE, clean up focus/drag and redraw when a client drops,
+    and route stdout/stderr through a writer that prefixes each log line
+    with a local timestamp.
+
+<a href=tree-f6362a6.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
+index 988dd9f..2810022 100644
+--- a/README.md
++++ b/README.md
+@@ -135,7 +135,7 @@ All server messages are written to a default log file:
+ - `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/bgce/bgce.log` (if `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is set)
+ - otherwise `~/.cache/bgce/bgce.log`
+ 
+-The path is printed to the terminal you used to start `bgce` so you know where to look (`tail -f` it, etc.). All `[BGCE]` output after that point goes into the log file.
++The path is printed to the terminal you used to start `bgce` so you know where to look (`tail -f` it, etc.). All server stdout/stderr after that point goes into the log file, with each line prefixed by a local timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm`).
+ 
+ 
+ ### Config File Format

+ 	       server.zoom, server.pan_x, server.pan_y);
+ }
+ 
++void client_disconnected(struct Client* c)
++{
++	if (!c)
++		return;
++	if (drag.active &amp;&amp; drag.target == c) {
++		drag.active = 0;
++		drag.target = NULL;
++		drag.dx = 0;
++		drag.dy = 0;
++		drag.acc_x = 0;
++		drag.acc_y = 0;
++		set_cursor_type(BGCE_CURSOR_DEFAULT);
++		printf("[BGCE] Drag cancelled (client disconnected).\n");
++	}
++}
++
+ int init_input(void) {
+ 	count = 0;
+ 	drag.active = 0;

+--- a/libbgce.c
++++ b/libbgce.c
+@@ -194,7 +194,9 @@ ssize_t bgce_send_msg(int conn, struct BGCEMessage* msg) {
+ 
+ 	ssize_t n = write(conn, msg, size);
+ 	if (n &lt; 0) {
+-		if (errno == EINTR)
++		/* EPIPE/ECONNRESET: peer gone — caller should drop the client.
++		 * With SIGPIPE ignored on the server, this is a normal path. */
++		if (errno != EPIPE &amp;&amp; errno != ECONNRESET &amp;&amp; errno != EINTR)
+ 			perror("[BGCE] write");
+ 		return -1;
+ 	}

+ 
+ 	client-&gt;fd = client_fd;
+

++		close(client_fd);
++		free(client);
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
+ 	// Add client to the linked list
+ 	client-&gt;next = server.clients;
+ 	client-&gt;z = server.clients-&gt;z + 1;
+@@ -48,6 +56,7 @@ void* client_thread(void* arg) {
+ 		struct BGCEMessage msg;

++			/* Crash, exit, or clean close — never tear down the server. */
+ 			printf("[BGCE] Client disconnected (fd=%d)\n", client_fd);

+ 		}
+@@ -203,6 +212,9 @@ void* client_thread(void* arg) {
+ 		}
+ 	}
+ 
++	/* Stop any in-progress drag that targets this client (UAF otherwise). */

++
+ 	if (client-&gt;buffer) {
+ 		munmap(client-&gt;buffer, client-&gt;width * client-&gt;height * 4);
+ 		client-&gt;buffer = NULL;
+@@ -210,7 +222,7 @@ void* client_thread(void* arg) {
+ 		client-&gt;shm_name[0] = '\0';
+ 	}
+ 
+-	// Remove client from the linked list
++	// Remove client from the linked list (never drop the background client)
+ 	struct Client* prev = NULL;
+ 	struct Client* curr = server.clients;
+ 	while (curr) {
+@@ -218,6 +230,7 @@ void* client_thread(void* arg) {
+ 			if (prev) {

+ 				server.clients = curr-&gt;next;
+ 			}
+ 			break;
+@@ -227,16 +240,17 @@ void* client_thread(void* arg) {
+ 	}
+ 
+ 	if (server.focused_client == client) {
+-		/* notify focused client it lost focus before we clear */
+-		struct BGCEMessage lost = {0};
+-		lost.type = MSG_FOCUS_CHANGE;
+-		lost.data.focus_event.state = 0;
+-		bgce_send_msg(client-&gt;fd, &amp;lost);
++		/* Socket is already dead — do not write a focus-lost message. */
+ 		server.focused_client = NULL;
+ 	}
+-	close(client-&gt;fd);
+ 
+-	printf("[BGCE] Thread exiting for client fd=%d\n", client-&gt;fd);
++	close(client_fd);
++	client-&gt;fd = -1;
++
++	/* Erase the window from the display; safe with only the background left. */
++	redraw_all(&amp;server);
++
++	printf("[BGCE] Client thread finished (fd=%d); server still running\n", client_fd);
+ 	free(client);
+ 	return NULL;
+ }
+diff --git a/server.c b/server.c

+--- a/server.c
++++ b/server.c
+@@ -5,12 +5,14 @@
+ #include &lt;fcntl.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;pthread.h&gt;

++#include &lt;time.h&gt;

+ struct ServerState server = {}; /* Global server state */
+@@ -25,6 +27,50 @@ static void ensure_dir(const char *path) {
+ }
+ 
+ static char listen_sock_path[BGCE_SOCKPATH_MAX];
++static char log_file_path[512];
++
++/* Read lines from a pipe and append them to the log with timestamps. */
++static void *log_timestamp_thread(void *arg)
++{
++	int rfd = (int)(intptr_t)arg;
++	int out_fd;
++	FILE *in;
++	char line[8192];
++
++	out_fd = open(log_file_path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND, 0600);
++	if (out_fd &lt; 0) {
++		close(rfd);
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
++	in = fdopen(rfd, "r");
++	if (!in) {
++		close(rfd);
++		close(out_fd);
++		return NULL;
++	}
++
++	/* Line-buffered so multi-thread printf interleaving is less chaotic */
++	while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), in)) {
++		struct timespec ts;
++		struct tm tm;
++		char stamp[40];
++
++		if (clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &amp;ts) != 0)
++			ts.tv_sec = time(NULL), ts.tv_nsec = 0;
++		if (!localtime_r(&amp;ts.tv_sec, &amp;tm)) {
++			dprintf(out_fd, "%s", line);
++			continue;
++		}
++		/* ISO-like local time with milliseconds */
++		strftime(stamp, sizeof(stamp), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", &amp;tm);
++		dprintf(out_fd, "%s.%03ld %s", stamp, ts.tv_nsec / 1000000L, line);
++	}
++
++	fclose(in); /* closes rfd */
++	close(out_fd);
++	return NULL;
++}
+

+ 	(void)sig;
+@@ -42,6 +88,9 @@ static void setup_log_file(void) {
+ 	const char *xdg = getenv("XDG_CACHE_HOME");
+ 	const char *home = getenv("HOME");
+ 	char dir[512];
++	int pipefd[2];

+

+@@ -57,31 +106,59 @@ static void setup_log_file(void) {

+-	int fd = open(log_path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND, 0600);

++	if (pipe(pipefd) &lt; 0) {

++		int fd = open(log_file_path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND, 0600);
++		if (fd &gt;= 0) {
++			dup2(fd, STDOUT_FILENO);
++			dup2(fd, STDERR_FILENO);
++			close(fd);
++		}
+ 		return;
++	}
+ 
+-	/* Tell the user (on their original terminal) where logs are going */
+-	dprintf(STDERR_FILENO, "[BGCE] Logging to %s\n", log_path);
++	pthread_attr_init(&amp;attr);
++	pthread_attr_setdetachstate(&amp;attr, PTHREAD_CREATE_DETACHED);
++	if (pthread_create(&amp;tid, &amp;attr, log_timestamp_thread,
++	                   (void *)(intptr_t)pipefd[0]) != 0) {

++		close(pipefd[0]);
++		close(pipefd[1]);

+commit fb1aa0b
+parent <a href=commit-6016e01.html>6016e01</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-10T11:42:49-03:00
+
+    Restore original window-move damage path.
+
+    L-shaped expose only: underlay stack bottom-to-top in the strips, then
+    full blit of the mover from its buffer at the new place. Drop FB scroll
+    of the window body and full-stack recompose of old∪new. Document in
+    redraw_region(), server.h, and AGENTS.md.
+
+<a href=tree-fb1aa0b.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/AGENTS.md b/AGENTS.md
+index 51dfd99..2ddf63e 100644
+--- a/AGENTS.md
++++ b/AGENTS.md
+@@ -19,7 +19,10 @@ Implement a minimal Linux graphical environment that runs without root, manages
+ - **MSG_DRAW:** Blit only the client that asked, clipped by opaque windows
+   above (subtract their rects). Do **not** full-stack recompose wallpaper /
+   clients below on ordinary draw — that was a regression (blink/refill).
+-  Full stack is for erase/move expose/pan/zoom only.
++- **Window move:** L-shaped expose only → underlay stack (bottom→top) in those
++  strips; then full blit of the moving client from its buffer. No FB scroll
++  of the window body; no full-stack recompose of old∪new.
++  Full stack remains for erase / pan edges / zoom.
+ - **Focus Handling:** Server tracks which client receives keyboard/mouse events.
+ - **Event Model:** Blocking reads (no polling); async draw calls.
+ - **Security:** Clients are sandboxed via file descriptors; no root operations.
+diff --git a/display.c b/display.c
+index 027d302..eeb8c34 100644
+--- a/display.c
++++ b/display.c
+@@ -1194,84 +1194,6 @@ static void composite_behind_rect(struct ServerState *srv, struct Client *behind
+ 	composite_chain_to_rect(srv, behind, x0, y0, x1, y1);
+ }
+ 
+-/*
+- * Slide a screen rect by (sdx,sdy). Overlap-safe. Source is [x0,x1)×[y0,y1).
+- */
+-static void fb_copy_rect_delta(struct ServerState *srv,
+-                               int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1,
+-                               int sdx, int sdy)
+-{
+-	uint32_t *fb;
+-	uint32_t sp;
+-	int sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1, dx0, dy0, w, h, y;
+-
+-	if (!srv || !srv-&gt;framebuffer || (sdx == 0 &amp;&amp; sdy == 0))
+-		return;
+-
+-	sx0 = x0;
+-	sy0 = y0;
+-	sx1 = x1;
+-	sy1 = y1;
+-	if (!clip_to_display(srv, &amp;sx0, &amp;sy0, &amp;sx1, &amp;sy1))
+-		return;
+-
+-	dx0 = sx0 + sdx;
+-	dy0 = sy0 + sdy;
+-	{
+-		int dx1 = sx1 + sdx, dy1 = sy1 + sdy;
+-		int max_sx0 = sx0, max_sy0 = sy0, min_sx1 = sx1, min_sy1 = sy1;
+-		if (dx0 &gt; max_sx0 + sdx) { /* keep for clarity */ }
+-		if (dx0 - sdx &gt; max_sx0)
+-			max_sx0 = dx0 - sdx;
+-		if (dy0 - sdy &gt; max_sy0)
+-			max_sy0 = dy0 - sdy;
+-		if (dx1 - sdx &lt; min_sx1)
+-			min_sx1 = dx1 - sdx;
+-		if (dy1 - sdy &lt; min_sy1)
+-			min_sy1 = dy1 - sdy;
+-		/* Also clip dest into display */
+-		if (dx0 &lt; 0) {
+-			max_sx0 += -dx0;
+-			dx0 = 0;
+-		}
+-		if (dy0 &lt; 0) {
+-			max_sy0 += -dy0;
+-			dy0 = 0;
+-		}
+-		if (dx0 + (min_sx1 - max_sx0) &gt; (int)srv-&gt;display_w)
+-			min_sx1 = max_sx0 + ((int)srv-&gt;display_w - dx0);
+-		if (dy0 + (min_sy1 - max_sy0) &gt; (int)srv-&gt;display_h)
+-			min_sy1 = max_sy0 + ((int)srv-&gt;display_h - dy0);
+-		sx0 = max_sx0;
+-		sy0 = max_sy0;
+-		sx1 = min_sx1;
+-		sy1 = min_sy1;
+-		if (sx0 &gt;= sx1 || sy0 &gt;= sy1)
+-			return;
+-		dx0 = sx0 + sdx;
+-		dy0 = sy0 + sdy;
+-		w = sx1 - sx0;
+-		h = sy1 - sy0;
+-	}
+-
+-	fb = (uint32_t *)srv-&gt;framebuffer;
+-	sp = display_stride_px(srv);
+-
+-	if (sdy &gt; 0 || (sdy == 0 &amp;&amp; sdx &gt; 0)) {
+-		for (y = h - 1; y &gt;= 0; y--) {
+-			uint32_t *src = fb + (sy0 + y) * (int)sp + sx0;
+-			uint32_t *dst = fb + (dy0 + y) * (int)sp + dx0;
+-			memmove(dst, src, (size_t)w * sizeof(uint32_t));
+-		}
+-	} else {
+-		for (y = 0; y &lt; h; y++) {
+-			uint32_t *src = fb + (sy0 + y) * (int)sp + sx0;
+-			uint32_t *dst = fb + (dy0 + y) * (int)sp + dx0;
+-			memmove(dst, src, (size_t)w * sizeof(uint32_t));
+-		}
+-	}
+-}

+ void redraw_all(struct ServerState* srv) {
+ 	if (!srv || !srv-&gt;framebuffer)
+ 		return;
+@@ -1475,21 +1397,40 @@ void draw(struct ServerState *srv, struct Client *cli)
+ }
+ 
+ /*
+- * Move a client on screen by (wdx, wdy) world pixels.
+- * `c` is still at the old position; caller updates x/y after.
++ * Window move — design (initial BGCE model; do not “optimize” with FB scroll
++ * of the whole window or full-stack recompose of old∪new):
++ *
++ * Caller: `c` is still at the OLD world position; apply (wdx,wdy) after.
++ *
++ *   1. Split the L-shaped expose: parts of the OLD screen rect that the
++ *      window no longer covers after the move (axis strips when size is
++ *      unchanged; old minus new when size changes).
++ *   2. For each L strip only: composite bottom → top from clients *under*
++ *      the mover (`c-&gt;next` … wallpaper). Small area, full underlay stack.
++ *   3. For the moving client itself: blit it FULL from its buffer at the
++ *      NEW position.  Do NOT re-walk windows under that body — only the
++ *      drawer’s pixels.  (Same spirit as MSG_DRAW’s “only me”.)
++ *   4. Re-blit windows stacked *above* the mover over old∪new so we never
++ *      paint over them.
+  *
+- * Fast path: FB scroll + L-shaped expose (classic).  sdx/sdy from actual
+- * screen bounds so strips match.  Then blit window from buffer at new pos.
+- * If screen size changed (odd zoom), fall back to union recompose.
++ * Forbidden regressions:
++ *   - fb_copy_rect_delta / FB scroll of the window body (looks fast, trails
++ *     and wrong underlay; was mislabeled “fast path”).
++ *   - composite_chain over the entire union of old and new for a move.
+  */
+-void redraw_region(struct ServerState* srv, struct Client* c, int wdx, int wdy) {
++void redraw_region(struct ServerState *srv, struct Client *c, int wdx, int wdy)
++{
+ 	struct Client moved;
+-	struct Client* p;
++	struct Client *p;
+ 	int ox0, oy0, ox1, oy1;
+ 	int nx0, ny0, nx1, ny1;
+ 	int sdx, sdy;
+ 	int ow, oh, nw, nh;
+ 	int ux0, uy0, ux1, uy1;
++	int bx0, by0, bx1, by1;
++	int expose[4][4];
++	int nexp = 0;
++	int i;
+ 
+ 	if (!srv || !srv-&gt;framebuffer || !c) {
+ 		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] Redraw: Invalid server, framebuffer, or client\n");
+@@ -1506,7 +1447,8 @@ void redraw_region(struct ServerState* srv, struct Client* c, int wdx, int wdy)
+ 
+ 	sdx = nx0 - ox0;
+ 	sdy = ny0 - oy0;
+-	if (sdx == 0 &amp;&amp; sdy == 0)
++	if (sdx == 0 &amp;&amp; sdy == 0 &amp;&amp;
++	    (ox1 - ox0) == (nx1 - nx0) &amp;&amp; (oy1 - oy0) == (ny1 - ny0))
+ 		return;
+ 
+ 	ow = ox1 - ox0;
+@@ -1515,52 +1457,56 @@ void redraw_region(struct ServerState* srv, struct Client* c, int wdx, int wdy)
+ 	nh = ny1 - ny0;
+ 
+ 	cursor_fb_begin();
+-	/* Move path may scroll FB pixels; always lift glyph first. */
+ 	(void)cursor_lift_all_ret();
+ 
++	/* ---- 1–2. L-shaped (or old\\new) expose: underlay only ---- */
+ 	if (ow == nw &amp;&amp; oh == nh) {
+-		/* L-shape: scroll body, fill exposed strips only. */
+-		fb_copy_rect_delta(srv, ox0, oy0, ox1, oy1, sdx, sdy);
+-
++		/* Classic L strips from translation of a fixed-size box. */
+ 		if (sdx &gt; 0) {
+ 			int ex1 = ox0 + sdx;
+ 			if (ex1 &gt; ox1)
+ 				ex1 = ox1;
+-			composite_behind_rect(srv, c-&gt;next, ox0, oy0, ex1, oy1);
++			if (ox0 &lt; ex1)
++				composite_behind_rect(srv, c-&gt;next, ox0, oy0, ex1, oy1);
+ 		} else if (sdx &lt; 0) {
+ 			int ex0 = ox1 + sdx;
+ 			if (ex0 &lt; ox0)
+ 				ex0 = ox0;
+-			composite_behind_rect(srv, c-&gt;next, ex0, oy0, ox1, oy1);
++			if (ex0 &lt; ox1)
++				composite_behind_rect(srv, c-&gt;next, ex0, oy0, ox1, oy1);
+ 		}
+ 		if (sdy &gt; 0) {
+ 			int ey1 = oy0 + sdy;
+ 			if (ey1 &gt; oy1)
+ 				ey1 = oy1;
+-			composite_behind_rect(srv, c-&gt;next, ox0, oy0, ox1, ey1);
++			if (oy0 &lt; ey1)
++				composite_behind_rect(srv, c-&gt;next, ox0, oy0, ox1, ey1);
+ 		} else if (sdy &lt; 0) {
+ 			int ey0 = oy1 + sdy;
+ 			if (ey0 &lt; oy0)
+ 				ey0 = oy0;
+-			composite_behind_rect(srv, c-&gt;next, ox0, ey0, ox1, oy1);
+-		}
+-
+-		{
+-			int bx0 = nx0, by0 = ny0, bx1 = nx1, by1 = ny1;
+-			if (clip_to_display(srv, &amp;bx0, &amp;by0, &amp;bx1, &amp;by1))
+-				blit_client_overlap(srv, &amp;moved, bx0, by0, bx1, by1);
++			if (ey0 &lt; oy1)
++				composite_behind_rect(srv, c-&gt;next, ox0, ey0, ox1, oy1);
+ 		}
+ 	} else {
+-		ux0 = ox0 &lt; nx0 ? ox0 : nx0;
+-		uy0 = oy0 &lt; ny0 ? oy0 : ny0;
+-		ux1 = ox1 &gt; nx1 ? ox1 : nx1;
+-		uy1 = oy1 &gt; ny1 ? oy1 : ny1;
+-		if (clip_to_display(srv, &amp;ux0, &amp;uy0, &amp;ux1, &amp;uy1)) {

++		nexp = rect_subtract(ox0, oy0, ox1, oy1, nx0, ny0, nx1, ny1,
++		                     expose, 4);
++		for (i = 0; i &lt; nexp; i++)

++			                      expose[i][0], expose[i][1],
++			                      expose[i][2], expose[i][3]);
+ 	}
+ 
++	/* ---- 3. Moving client: full buffer blit at new place only ---- */
++	bx0 = nx0;
++	by0 = ny0;
++	bx1 = nx1;
++	by1 = ny1;
++	if (clip_to_display(srv, &amp;bx0, &amp;by0, &amp;bx1, &amp;by1))

++	/* ---- 4. Windows above: redraw over old∪new ---- */
+ 	ux0 = ox0 &lt; nx0 ? ox0 : nx0;
+ 	uy0 = oy0 &lt; ny0 ? oy0 : ny0;
+ 	ux1 = ox1 &gt; nx1 ? ox1 : nx1;

+parent <a href=commit-289763f.html>289763f</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-03T13:36:00-03:00
+
+    Install into flat /bin /lib /include for lin0.
+
+    Default to cc, libdrm under /include/libdrm, and make ldconfig optional so make install works on musl without /usr.
+
+<a href=tree-fb43a29.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/Makefile b/Makefile
+index 7f68e71..8fa42ec 100644
+--- a/Makefile
++++ b/Makefile
+@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
+-CC = gcc
+-CFLAGS = -Wall -O1 -std=c99 -fPIC -g -I/usr/include/libdrm -I.
+-LDFLAGS = -lrt -ldrm -lm
++CC ?= cc
++CFLAGS ?= -Wall -O1 -std=c99 -fPIC -g -I/include/libdrm -I.
++LDFLAGS ?= -lrt -ldrm -lm
+ 
+ SERVER_OBJS = server.o loop.o libbgce.so input.o display.o config.o
+ LIB_OBJS = libbgce.o
+@@ -22,9 +22,9 @@ client: client.c bgce.h
+ clean:
+ 	rm -f *.o bgce libbgce.so client app
+ 
+-INSTALL_BIN = /usr/bin
+-INSTALL_LIB = /usr/lib
+-INSTALL_INCLUDE = /usr/include
++INSTALL_BIN = /bin
++INSTALL_LIB = /lib
++INSTALL_INCLUDE = /include
+ 
+ .PHONY: install
+ install: bgce libbgce.so bgce.h
+@@ -34,7 +34,7 @@ install: bgce libbgce.so bgce.h
+ 	install -m 755 libbgce.so $(INSTALL_LIB)
+ 	install -d $(INSTALL_INCLUDE)
+ 	install -m 644 bgce.h $(INSTALL_INCLUDE)
+-	ldconfig
++	-ldconfig 2&gt;/dev/null || true
+ 
+ SERVER_LOG ?= server.log
+ SERVER_PID ?= server.pid
+diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
+index 08dd178..8b0a365 100644
+--- a/README.md
++++ b/README.md
+@@ -78,15 +78,20 @@ I also posted a video on my blog:
+ 
+ ## Build Instructions
+ 
++On lin0 use `/bin/cc` and install into the flat root (`/bin`, `/lib`, `/include` — no `/usr`):
++
+ ```bash
+ git clone &lt;repo-url&gt;
+-cd BGCE
+-make all client
++cd bgce
++make CC=cc CFLAGS='-Wall -O1 -std=c99 -fPIC -I/include/libdrm -I.' all client
++make install
+ ./bgce   # Start server
+ # Go to a different tty
+ ./client  # Start test client
+ ```
+ 
++Needs userspace `libdrm` headers in `/include/libdrm` and `libdrm.so` in `/lib`.
++
+ 
+ ## Configuration
+ 
+</pre>

diff --git a/www/commit-ffb3dd9.html b/www/commit-ffb3dd9.html
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..80af5aa
--- /dev/null
+++ b/www/commit-ffb3dd9.html
@@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+<!DOCTYPE html>
+<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
+<title>bgce ffb3dd9</title>
+<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
+<link rel=icon href=data:,>
+<style>pre{width:52ch;margin:2ch auto;white-space:pre-wrap}a{color:#ff00ff}</style>
+<pre>
+<a href=index.html>bgce</a> / <b>commit</b>
+
+<a href=log.html>log</a> | <a href=tree.html>tree</a> | <a href=refs.html>refs</a>
+
+commit ffb3dd9
+parent <a href=commit-3c41f5e.html>3c41f5e</a> 
+author Brian Mayer &lt;bleemayer@gmail.com&gt;
+date   2026-07-08T14:11:14-03:00
+
+    Always restore VT keyboard mode on exit so the tty is not frozen.
+
+    Leaving K_OFF when KDGKBMODE failed at startup meant quit only set
+    KD_TEXT and the console stayed keyboard-dead. Track K_OFF, fall back
+    to K_XLATE, and re-open /dev/tty if needed during release.
+
+<a href=tree-ffb3dd9.html>tree</a>
+
+<b>diff</b>
+
+diff --git a/display.c b/display.c
+index 3bb1b53..e7ccbe9 100644
+--- a/display.c
++++ b/display.c
+@@ -26,10 +26,15 @@ extern struct config config;
+ static int vt_fd = -1;
+ /* Previous KDSKBMODE so we can restore on exit (KDGKBMODE uses long). */
+ static long vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
++/* 1 if we successfully set K_OFF and must undo it even when KDGKBMODE failed. */
++static int vt_kb_off_active;
+ #ifndef K_OFF
+ /* Disabled keyboard → console (Linux ≥ 2.6.39). */
+ #define K_OFF 0x04
+ #endif
++#ifndef K_XLATE
++#define K_XLATE 0x00
++#endif
+ 
+ #if CURSOR_WIDTH != 32 || CURSOR_HEIGHT != 32
+ #error "software cursor blit assumes CURSOR_WIDTH/HEIGHT == 32"
+@@ -504,9 +509,11 @@ int setup_vt_handling(void) {
+ 		return -1;
+ 	}
+ 
++	vt_kb_off_active = 0;
+ 	vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
+ 	if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDGKBMODE, &amp;vt_saved_kbmode) &lt; 0) {
+-		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDGKBMODE failed: %s\n",
++		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDGKBMODE failed: %s "
++		        "(will restore K_XLATE on exit)\n",
+ 		        strerror(errno));
+ 		vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
+ 	}
+@@ -530,6 +537,7 @@ int setup_vt_handling(void) {
+ 		        "(keys may still reach the tty)\n",
+ 		        strerror(errno));
+ 	} else {
++		vt_kb_off_active = 1;
+ 		printf("[BGCE] VT: KD_GRAPHICS + keyboard off "
+ 		       "(input via /dev/input only)\n");
+ 	}
+@@ -537,25 +545,56 @@ int setup_vt_handling(void) {
+ 	return 0;
+ }
+ 
++/*
++ * Always put the console back to a usable state.  Leaving K_OFF active
++ * freezes the tty (no keyboard) after quit — that was the exit bug.
++ */
+ void release_vt(void) {
+-	if (vt_fd &lt; 0)
+-		return;
++	int fd = vt_fd;
++	long mode;
++
++	/* Re-open if needed so we can still recover after a partial teardown. */
++	if (fd &lt; 0) {
++		fd = open("/dev/tty", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
++		if (fd &lt; 0)
++			fd = open("/dev/tty0", O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC);
++		if (fd &lt; 0)
++			return;
++	}
+ 
+-	if (vt_saved_kbmode &gt;= 0) {
+-		if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDSKBMODE, vt_saved_kbmode) &lt; 0)
+-			fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: restore KDSKBMODE failed: %s\n",
+-			        strerror(errno));
+-		vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
++	/*
++	 * Prefer the saved mode; never restore K_OFF.  If we never saw a
++	 * mode (KDGKBMODE failed), fall back to K_XLATE so the shell works.
++	 * K_XLATE is 0 — do not use "&gt;= 0" alone as a "valid" flag.
++	 */
++	if (vt_saved_kbmode &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; vt_saved_kbmode != (long)K_OFF)
++		mode = vt_saved_kbmode;
++	else
++		mode = (long)K_XLATE;
++
++	/* Keyboard first so the console can accept input as soon as text is on. */
++	if (vt_kb_off_active || vt_saved_kbmode &gt;= 0) {
++		if (ioctl(fd, KDSKBMODE, mode) &lt; 0) {
++			fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: restore KDSKBMODE %ld failed: %s; "
++			        "trying K_XLATE\n",
++			        mode, strerror(errno));
++			if (ioctl(fd, KDSKBMODE, (long)K_XLATE) &lt; 0)
++				fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: K_XLATE restore failed: %s\n",
++				        strerror(errno));
++		}
+ 	}
+ 
+-	if (ioctl(vt_fd, KDSETMODE, KD_TEXT) &lt; 0)
++	if (ioctl(fd, KDSETMODE, KD_TEXT) &lt; 0)
+ 		fprintf(stderr, "[BGCE] VT: KDSETMODE KD_TEXT failed: %s\n",
+ 		        strerror(errno));
+ 	else
+ 		printf("[BGCE] VT: restored KD_TEXT + keyboard mode\n");
+ 
+-	close(vt_fd);
+-	vt_fd = -1;
++	if (fd == vt_fd)
++		vt_fd = -1;
++	close(fd);
++	vt_saved_kbmode = -1;
++	vt_kb_off_active = 0;
+ }
+ 
+ /* ------------------------------------------------------------------
+</pre>
